claims.evidence: The claim is supported by immunohistochemistry data presented in Figure 5A-F.

claims.claim: Protein expression of TGF-β1 and α-MSH almost disappeared in the epithelium of hair follicles co-cultured with autologous ILC1lc or CD8+/NKG2D+ cells.
claims.source: Notably, quantitative immunohistomorphoemtry (qIHM) also showed that protein expression of the immunoinhibitory HF-IP guardians, TGF-β1 and α-MSH (Gilhar et al., 2012; Bertolini et al., 2020; Paus et al., 2018; Ito et al., 2004), almost disappeared in the epithelium of HFs co-cultured with autologous ILC1lc or CD8+/NKG2D+ cells (=positive control) (Figure 5G, H and I)
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by quantitative immunohistomorphometry data presented in Figure 5G-I.

claims.claim: Adding anti-NKG2D blocking antibodies prevented hair follicle immune privilege collapse and preserved the immune privilege in the ILC1lc /NKG2D treated group.
claims.source: Importantly, adding anti-NKG2D blocking antibodies prevented HFs IP collapse and preserved the IP in the ILC1lc /NKG2D treated group (Figure 5G, H and I).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by immunohistochemistry data presented in Figure 5G-I.

claims.claim: ILC1lc significantly accelerated the transformation of anagen into catagen hair follicles ex vivo compared to ILC2, ILC3, or PBMCs/PHA.
claims.source: This showed that ILC1lc significantly accelerated the transformation of anagen into catagen HFs ex vivo (Paus et al., 2005) compared to all three negative controls (ILC2, ILC3, or PBMCs/PHA) – thus eliciting the third hallmark of the AA phenotype besides HF-IP collapse and dystrophy ex vivo (Gilhar et al., 2012; Bertolini et al., 2020; Messenger et al., 1986; Figure 6A)
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by hair cycle analysis data presented in Figure 6A.

claims.claim: ILC1lc produced and secreted higher amounts of IFN-γ into the medium than all other cells co-cultured with 'stressed' hair follicles, including CD8+/NKG2D+ cells.
claims.source: ELISA analysis revealed that ILC1lc produced and secreted higher amounts of IFN-γ into the medium than all other cells co-cultured with 'stressed' HFs, including CD8+/NKG2D+ cells (p<0.05) (Figure 6B).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by ELISA data presented in Figure 6B.

claims.claim: ILC1lc showed significantly increased intracellular IFN-γ expression when co-cultured with 'stressed,' autologous hair follicles.
claims.source: FACS analysis showed ILC1lc activation when these were co-cultured with 'stressed,' autologous HFs (600 cells/HF), as evidenced by significantly increased intracellular IFN-γ expression by ILC1lc (Bernink et al., 2017) (93 ± 11%) compared to the positive control (CD8+/NKG2D+, 75 ± 9%, p<0.05) (Figure 6C)
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by FACS analysis data presented in Figure 6C.

claims.claim: Neutralizing anti-IFN-γ antibodies significantly reduced premature catagen development of hair follicles co-cultured with ILC1lc.
claims.source: When neutralizing anti- IFN-γ antibodies were administered into the medium of the organ culture, premature catagen development of HFs co-cultured with ILC1lc was significantly reduced (Figure 6A), strongly suggesting that premature catagen induction by ILC1lc depends on their IFN-γsecretion (Seillet et al., 2021).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by hair cycle analysis data presented in Figure 6A.

claims.claim: Reduced catagen induction was observed after adding NKG2D-blocking antibodies to the medium of hair follicles co-cultured with ILC1lc.
claims.source: Importantly, reduced catagen induction was also seen after adding NKG2D-blocking antibodies to the medium (Figure 6A).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by hair cycle analysis data presented in Figure 6A.

claims.claim: ILC1lc activation and IFN-γ secretion are induced by NKG2D-stimulating danger signals overexpressed by stressed hair follicle epithelium, such as MICA.
claims.source: This suggests that ILC1lc activation and IFN-γsecretion are induced by NKG2D-stimulating danger signals overexpressed by stressed HF epithelium, such as MICA.
claims.evidence: This is an inference based on the experimental results showing that NKG2D blocking reduces ILC1lc effects.

claims.claim: Significant AA-like hair loss was observed macroscopically in the xenotransplants injected with ILC1lc compared to the negative control, at about the same level as positive control xenotransplants.
claims.source: When measured 45 days later, significant AA-like hair loss was observed macroscopically in the xenotransplants injected with ILC1lc compared to the negative control, at about the same level as positive control xenotransplants (Figure 7A).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by macroscopic hair count data presented in Figure 7A.

claims.claim: Anti-CD3/OKT3 antibodies failed to abrogate hair loss induction in mice treated with ILC1lc alone.
claims.source: This showed that anti-CD3 failed to abrogate hair loss induction in the mice treated with ILC1lc alone, but suppressed hair loss in the group treated with enriched CD8/NKG2D cells, as expected (Figure 7—figure supplement 1A).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by in vivo experimental data presented in Figure 7—figure supplement 1A.

claims.claim: Anti-CD3/OKT3 antibodies suppressed hair loss in the group treated with enriched CD8/NKG2D cells.
claims.source: This showed that anti-CD3 failed to abrogate hair loss induction in the mice treated with ILC1lc alone, but suppressed hair loss in the group treated with enriched CD8/NKG2D cells, as expected (Figure 7—figure supplement 1A).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by in vivo experimental data presented in Figure 7—figure supplement 1A.

claims.claim: ILC1lc induced hair follicle dystrophy, miniaturization and perifollicular lymphocytic infiltrate around anagen hair follicles in vivo.
claims.source: Immunohistology revealed that ILC1lc, just like autologous enriched CD8/NKG2D cells, induced a phenocopy of AA immunopathology in previously healthy human scalp skin in vivo, in sharp contrast to the negative control PBMCs/PHA group: HFs dystrophy, miniaturization and perifollicular lymphocytic infiltrate around anagen HFs (Figure 7B)
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by histology data presented in Figure 7B.

claims.claim: ILC1lc induced immune privilege collapse in vivo, characterized by significantly increased expression of HLA-A,B,C, β2 MG, and HLA-DR of the hair follicle epithelium, along with downregulation of α-MSH and TGF-β1.
claims.source: as well as induction of HF-IP collapse (significantly increased expression of HLA-A,B,C, β2 MG, and HLA-DR of the HF epithelium, along with downregulation of the immune privilege guardians, α-MSH and TGF-β1) (Figure 7C and D).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by immunohistochemistry data presented in Figure 7C-F.

claims.claim: IFN-γ+ cells were found to be increased around the bulb of xenotransplants injected with ILC1lc.
claims.source: In line with the key role of IFN-γ in the development of AA (Gilhar et al., 2012; Gilhar et al., 2019a), IFN-γ+ cells were found to be increased around the bulb of xenotransplants injected with ILC1lc, even in the presence of the anti-CD3 antibody (OKT3), or with enriched CD8/NKG2D cells, but not with PHA-treated PBMCs or enriched CD8/NKG2D cells in the presence of OKT3 (Figure 7—figure supplement 1A,B,C,D,E,F and G and Figure 7—figure supplement 2A,B,C and D).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by immunohistochemistry data presented in Figure 7—figure supplement 1 and Figure 7—figure supplement 2.

claims.claim: Dense infiltration of ILC1lc was found only in xenotransplants treated with the purified ILC1lc.
claims.source: while dense infiltration of ILC1lc was found only in xenotransplants treated with the purified ILC1lc (Figure 7—figure supplement 3E and F).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by immunofluorescence data presented in Figure 7—figure supplement 3E-F.

claims.claim: The peri- and intrafollicular distribution and mean number of ILC1lc in human skin xenotransplants injected with enriched CD8/NKG2D cells imitated that of ILC1lc seen in spontaneously developed hair loss lesions of AA patients.
claims.source: Interestingly, qIHM also showed that the peri- and intrafollicular distribution and mean number of ILC1lc in human skin xenotransplants injected with enriched CD8/NKG2D cells imitated that of ILC1lc seen in spontaneously developed hair loss lesions of AA patients, further supporting the role of ILC1lc in human AA (Figure 1A, B, C and D, Figure 8A, B, C and D and Figure 1—figure supplement 1B).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by quantitative immunohistomorphometry data comparing patient samples (Figure 1) and xenotransplant samples (Figure 8).

claims.claim: CD8+/NKG2D+lymphocytes significantly outnumbered ILC1lc in the experimentally induced AA lesions.
claims.source: Yet, CD8+/NKG2D+lymphocytes significantly outnumbered ILC1lc in the experimentally induced AA lesions (p<0.01) (Figure 8E and F), just as they do in human AA patients (Figure 1E and F).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by quantitative immunohistomorphometry data presented in Figure 8E-F.

claims.claim: This study is the first to phenotypically and functionally explore the role of Eomes+ILC1lc in human AA in vivo and ex vivo.
claims.source: The current study is the first to phenotypically and functionally explore the role of Eomes +ILC1 lc in human AA in vivo and ex vivo.
claims.evidence: This is a claim about the novelty of the study, supported by the comprehensive experimental data presented.

claims.claim: ILC1lc provide the first functional evidence that expanded circulating autologous human ILC1lc suffice to induce all hallmarks of the AA hair loss phenotype in previously healthy, organ-cultured human scalp hair follicles ex vivo.
claims.source: Here, we show that ILC1lc are increased in AA lesions provide the first functional evidence that expanded circulating autologous human ILC1lc suffice to induce all hallmarks of the AA hair loss phenotype (premature catagen, HF dystrophy, and HF-IP collapse) in previously healthy, organ-cultured human scalp HFs ex vivo
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by the comprehensive ex vivo experimental data presented in Figures 3-6.

claims.claim: ILC1lc suffice to induce all hallmarks of the AA hair loss phenotype in human scalp skin xenotransplants in vivo.
claims.source: Here, we show that ILC1lc are increased in AA lesions provide the first functional evidence that expanded circulating autologous human ILC1lc suffice to induce all hallmarks of the AA hair loss phenotype (premature catagen, HF dystrophy, and HF-IP collapse) in previously healthy, organ-cultured human scalp HFs ex vivo and in human scalp skin xenotransplants in vivo, where they also cause the characteristic clinical hair loss phenomenon.
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by the in vivo experimental data presented in Figures 7-8.

claims.claim: This study provides the first unequivocal functional evidence of a key role of ILC1lc innate lymphocytes in a model human autoimmune disease.
claims.source: This also provides the first unequivocal functional evidence of a key role of ILC1lc innate lymphocytes in a model human autoimmune disease, and thus identifies these lymphocytes as important novel targets in future AA therapy.
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by the comprehensive experimental data showing ILC1lc can induce AA.

claims.claim: IFN-γ secretion and NKG2D signaling are both required for ILC1lc to induce AA-pattern hair follicle damage.
claims.source: Mechanistically, we demonstrate that IFN-γsecretion and NKG2D signaling are both required for this AA-pattern HF damage to occur (Figure 9).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data showing that blocking IFN-γ or NKG2D reduces ILC1lc effects (Figures 5-6).

claims.claim: ILC1lc interact directly with human hair follicles rather than affecting them only indirectly.
claims.source: That ILC1lc alone can induce all hallmarks of AA in a healthy human (mini-) organ ex vivo and in vivo, presumably in an autoantigen-independent manner, also demonstrates that these innate/transitional lymphocytes interact directly with human HFs, rather than affecting them only indirectly.
claims.evidence: This is an inference based on the experimental results showing ILC1lc alone can induce AA.

claims.claim: Resident T-cells in human scalp skin transplants are not responsible for the AA-inducing effects of ILC1lc in vivo.
claims.source: We also show that resident T-cells in human scalp skin transplants are not responsible for the AA-inducing effects of ILC1lc in vivo (Figure 7—figure supplement 1 and Figure 7—figure supplement 2).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data showing anti-CD3 antibodies do not prevent ILC1lc-induced AA (Figure 7—figure supplement 1).

claims.claim: CD8+ T cells are not the only drivers of AA disease.
claims.source: Our study demonstrates that CD8+ T cells, which have long been thought to represent the central players in AA pathobiology (Pratt et al., 2017; Xing et al., 2014; de Jong et al., 2018; Gilhar et al., 1998; Wang et al., 2016; Paus et al., 1993), are not the only drivers of disease (Gilhar et al., 2019a; Pratt et al., 2017; de Jong et al., 2018; Paus et al., 1993)
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by the experimental data showing ILC1lc alone can induce AA, and by citations to published literature.

claims.claim: The characteristic hair loss pattern diagnosed as AA phenotype does not always represent a classical, autoantigen- and autoreactive CD8+/NKGD2+T-cell-dependent autoimmune disease.
claims.source: The study further supports the concept that the characteristic hair loss pattern we diagnose as AA phenotype, does not always represent a classical, autoantigen- and autoreactive CD8+/NKGD2 +T-cell-dependent autoimmune disease ('autoimmune AA' [AAA]), but can also reflect non-autoimmune pathomechanisms that may perhaps best be defined as non-autoimmune AA subtype (NAIAA) (Bertolini et al., 2020; Paus et al., 2018; Figure 9).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by the experimental data and citations to published literature proposing the AAA/NAIAA distinction.

claims.claim: An AA-subtype that began as NAIAA can over time transform into the AAA-variant in a state of prolonged hair follicle immune privilege collapse.
claims.source: In a state of prolonged HF-IP collapse and thus chronic exposure of HF-associated autoantigens to (pre-existent?) autoreactive CD8 +T cells, it is well conceivable that an AA-subtype that began as NAIAA can over time transform into the AAA-variant, thus explaining the chronic-intermittent course that is seen in so many autoimmune diseases.
claims.evidence: This is a speculative inference based on the experimental findings and known features of autoimmune diseases.

claims.claim: The novel concept of ILC1-induced NAIAA mandates a differential, personalized management approach to future AA therapy.
claims.source: The novel concept of ILC1-induced NAIAA mandates a differential, personalized management approach to future AA therapy, which tailors treatment to the specific pathobiology at hand in any given AA patient.
claims.evidence: This is an inference and recommendation based on the study findings.

claims.claim: Future AA therapy must include the targeting of pathogenic, potently IFN-γ-secreting ILC1lc, at least when these are seen to be increased in lesional AA biopsies.
claims.source: This must now include the targeting of pathogenic, potently IFN-γ -secreting ILC1lc, at least when these are seen to be increased in lesional AA biopsies.
claims.evidence: This is a recommendation based on the study findings.

claims.source: In fact, we demonstrate here that ILC1lc are even more potent IFN-γproducers than CD8 +T cells.
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by ELISA and FACS data presented in Figure 6B-C.

claims.claim: The selective tissue distribution of ILC1lc makes them ideally localized to provide an early source of cytokines to initiate/trigger pro-inflammatory immune responses directed against distressed tissues.
claims.source: Also, despite the relatively low numbers of ILC1lc, their selective tissue distribution makes them ideally localized to provide an early source of cytokines to initiate/trigger pro-inflammatory immune responses directed against distressed tissues (Vivier, 2021), as documented here in our co-culture assay with 'stressed' human scalp HFs ex vivo.
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to published literature and the experimental data from the co-culture assay.

claims.claim: IL-12 and IL-18 may be involved in the early stages of AA development by stimulating IFN-γ production from resident IL-12Rß2+immune cells.
claims.source: That IL-12 and IL-18 were among the cytokines used here to facilitate ILC1lc isolation from human PBMCs is also interesting in the context of our most recent observation that local IL-12 signaling, supported by IL-18, may be involved in the early stages of AA development by stimulating IFN-γ production from resident IL-12Rß2+immune cells, eventually leading to HF-IP collapse (Edelkamp, 2021).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to published literature.

claims.claim: Treatment with IL-12 +IL-18 of healthy hair follicles selectively enriches IFN-γ-inducible genes and promotes the release of IFN-γ into the medium and thus hair follicle immune privilege collapse.
claims.source: In fact, treatment with IL-12 +IL-18 of healthy HFs selectively enriches IFN-γ -inducible genes and promotes the release of IFN-γ into the medium and thus HF-IP collapse.
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to published literature.

claims.claim: IL-12 is a key effector cytokine in promoting pathogenic IFN-γ secretion and hair follicle immune privilege collapse.
claims.source: These preliminary findings suggest that IL-12 is a key effector cytokine in promoting pathogenic IFN-γ secretion and HF-IP collapse.
claims.evidence: This is an inference based on cited literature and the experimental context.

claims.claim: An immunopathology-initiating role of ILC1lc has been proposed in vitiligo, inflammatory bowel disease, lupus erythematosus, and the aggravation of atherosclerosis.
claims.source: An immunopathology-initiating role of ILC1lc is not unique to AA and has also been proposed in other inflammatory conditions (Kim et al., 2021), including vitiligo (Tulic et al., 2019), which shares some pathogenesis features with AA (Harris, 2013; Tomaszewska et al., 2020), inflammatory bowel disease (McDonald et al., 2018; Bernink et al., 2013; Tang et al., 2019), lupus erythematosus (Guo et al., 2019), and the aggravation of atherosclerosis (Wu et al., 2018).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by citations to published literature.

claims.claim: This study is the first to demonstrate that ILC1lc can induce the full disease-mimicking immunopathology phenotype in a previously healthy human (mini-) organ.
claims.source: Yet, to the best of our knowledge, the current study is the first to demonstrate that these innate immunocytes can indeed induce the full disease-mimicking immunopathology phenotype in a previously healthy human (mini-) organ.
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by the comprehensive experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claims.claim: Abnormalities in the crosstalk between ILC1lc and gut microbiota have been observed in various diseases.
claims.source: Also, abnormalities in the crosstalk between ILC1lc and gut microbiota have been observed in various diseases (Jiao et al., 2020).
claims.evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to published literature.

claims.evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to published literature.

claims.claim: The study introduces IFN-γ-secreting ILC1lc lymphocytes as important novel players in human AA pathobiology and identifies them as new therapeutic intervention targets.
claims.source: Collectively, our study introduces IFN-γ -secreting ILC1lc lymphocytes as important novel players in human AA pathobiology and identifies them as new therapeutic intervention targets.
claims.evidence: This is a summary claim supported by all the experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claims.source: Their strategic location, their capability to recognize and respond to HF distress signals such as MICA and selected chemokines, the excessive production of IFN-γ by ILC1lc, and their direct, pathogenic effects on human HFs ex vivo documented here, all support that these cells play a hitherto unappreciated role in early AA pathogenesis.
claims.evidence: This is a summary claim supported by the experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claims.evidence: The claim is supported by the experimental data and a citation to published literature.

claims.evidence: The claim is supported by the experimental data presented in the manuscript.

results.result: ILC1lc are significantly increased in lesional and non-lesional AA hair follicles compared to healthy control skin, where they are extremely rare and preferentially located in the papillary dermis and around hair follicles.
results.evaluation: Claims C1, C54-C57 are supported by comprehensive immunofluorescence data using three different antibody combinations (Figure 1) and quantitative immunohistomorphometry showing statistically significant increases (p<0.01) in ILC1lc in both lesional and non-lesional AA skin compared to healthy controls. The data demonstrate appropriate controls and multiple independent markers.

results.result: ILC1lc can be expanded from human PBMCs and are characterized by a distinct phenotype: CD49a+CD49b-, lin-/CD127+/CD117-/CRTH2-, T-betlo/Eomeshi, positive for ILC1 markers (CD200R, CXCR6) and negative for classical NK markers (IRF8, Perforin, NKp80, CD16).
results.evaluation: Claims C8, C51-C53, C59-C65 are well-supported by FACS analysis data (Figure 2 and supplements) showing the phenotypic characterization of expanded ILC1lc. The study uses appropriate markers to distinguish ILC1lc from NK cells and ILC3s, with proper controls. However, the authors acknowledge ongoing controversy in the field about ILC1/NK distinction, which is appropriately discussed.

results.result: ILC1lc induce significant hair follicle cytotoxicity and dystrophy ex vivo, exceeding the effects of CD8+/NKG2D+ cells, as evidenced by LDH release, morphological changes, melanin clumping, decreased proliferation, and increased apoptosis.
results.evaluation: Claims C3, C66-C70 are supported by multiple complementary assays including LDH release (Figure 3), H&E staining (Figure 4A-C), Masson-Fontana histochemistry (Figure 4D-G), and Ki-67/TUNEL analysis (Figure 4H-K). The data show statistically significant differences (p<0.01 to p<0.001) compared to appropriate negative controls (ILC2, ILC3, PBMCs/PHA). Sample sizes appear adequate (n=15-24 HFs from 2-3 donors).

results.result: ILC1lc induce hair follicle immune privilege collapse ex vivo, characterized by upregulation of HLA-A,B,C, β2-microglobulin, HLA-DR, MICA, and CD1d, along with downregulation of immune privilege guardians TGF-β1 and α-MSH. This effect is prevented by NKG2D-blocking antibodies.
results.evaluation: Claims C4, C71-C74 are supported by immunohistochemistry data (Figure 5) showing statistically significant changes in immune privilege markers. The rescue experiment with anti-NKG2D antibodies provides mechanistic support. Sample sizes are adequate (n=9-12 HFs from three donors). The data are consistent with the known role of immune privilege collapse in AA pathogenesis.

results.result: ILC1lc induce premature catagen development in hair follicles ex vivo through IFN-γ secretion and NKG2D signaling. ILC1lc produce higher amounts of IFN-γ than CD8+/NKG2D+ cells, and both anti-IFN-γ and anti-NKG2D antibodies reduce catagen induction.
results.evaluation: Claims C2, C75-C80 are supported by hair cycle analysis (Figure 6A), ELISA data (Figure 6B), and FACS analysis (Figure 6C) showing statistically significant effects (p<0.05 to p<0.001). The antibody blocking experiments provide mechanistic evidence. However, C80 is an inference rather than direct demonstration, though it is a reasonable interpretation of the blocking data.

results.result: Intradermal injection of ILC1lc into healthy human scalp skin xenotransplants on SCID/beige mice induces characteristic AA lesions including hair loss, hair follicle dystrophy, immune privilege collapse, and increased IFN-γ+ cells. Anti-CD3 antibodies do not prevent ILC1lc-induced AA but do prevent CD8/NKG2D-induced AA.
results.evaluation: Claims C7, C81-C89 are supported by comprehensive in vivo data including macroscopic hair counts (Figure 7A), histology (Figure 7B), immunohistochemistry (Figures 7C-F and supplements), and quantitative analysis. The anti-CD3 experiments (Figure 7—figure supplement 1) provide critical evidence that resident T cells are not responsible for ILC1lc effects. Sample sizes appear adequate (n=5-9 xenotransplants per group). The xenotransplant model is well-established for AA research.

results.result: Both IFN-γ secretion and NKG2D signaling are mechanistically required for ILC1lc to induce AA-pattern hair follicle damage.
results.evaluation: Claims C5, C6, C94 are supported by antibody blocking experiments showing that both anti-NKG2D and anti-IFN-γ antibodies reduce ILC1lc-induced effects ex vivo (Figures 5 and 6A). The data demonstrate statistical significance and appropriate controls. However, the experiments do not fully dissect whether these pathways are independent or interdependent.

results.result: AA is not always an autoantigen-dependent, CD8+ T cell-driven autoimmune disease. ILC1lc alone can induce AA, supporting the existence of non-autoimmune AA variants (NAIAA).
results.evaluation: Claims C9, C97, C98, C113, C114 are supported by the comprehensive ex vivo and in vivo data showing ILC1lc alone can induce all hallmarks of AA. The anti-CD3 experiments (C82, C83) provide critical evidence that T cells are not required for ILC1lc-induced AA. However, the NAIAA concept (C98, C114) is partially inferential and relies on the assumption that ILC1lc act in an autoantigen-independent manner, which is not directly demonstrated.

results.result: This is the first study to demonstrate that ILC1lc can induce the full disease-mimicking immunopathology phenotype in a previously healthy human organ ex vivo and in vivo, providing the first functional evidence of a key role of ILC1lc in a model human autoimmune disease.
results.evaluation: Claims C90-C93, C108, C111 regarding novelty are supported by the comprehensive experimental data presented throughout the manuscript. The study provides the first functional demonstration that ILC1lc alone can induce all hallmarks of AA (cytotoxicity, immune privilege collapse, catagen induction) both ex vivo and in vivo. The novelty claims are appropriately contextualized with citations to prior literature.

results.result: ILC1lc are more potent IFN-γ producers than CD8+ T cells, and their selective tissue distribution makes them ideally positioned to initiate pro-inflammatory immune responses against distressed tissues.
results.evaluation: Claims C102 and C103 are supported by ELISA data (Figure 6B) showing statistically significant higher IFN-γ production by ILC1lc compared to CD8+/NKG2D+ cells (p<0.05), and FACS data (Figure 6C) showing higher intracellular IFN-γ expression. The tissue distribution claim is supported by immunofluorescence data (Figure 1) and citations to published literature.

results.result: ILC1lc may arrive at hair follicles before CD8+ T cells and interact directly with hair follicles rather than affecting them only indirectly. Their strategic location and capability to recognize hair follicle distress signals support a role in early AA pathogenesis.
results.evaluation: Claims C58, C95, C96, C112 are supported by data showing ILC1lc are increased in non-lesional AA skin (C57, Figure 1D) and that anti-CD3 antibodies do not prevent ILC1lc-induced AA (C82, Figure 7—figure supplement 1). However, C58 is explicitly stated as an inference ('may indicate'), and the temporal sequence is not directly demonstrated. The direct interaction claim (C95) is a reasonable inference from the ex vivo data but not definitively proven.

results.result: An AA subtype that begins as NAIAA may transform into AAA over time in a state of prolonged immune privilege collapse. This concept mandates a differential, personalized approach to AA therapy that includes targeting ILC1lc.
results.evaluation: Claims C99-C101 are speculative inferences and recommendations based on the study findings. C99 is explicitly presented as speculation ('it is well conceivable') without direct experimental support. C100 and C101 are recommendations for future therapy rather than experimental findings. While these are reasonable hypotheses based on the data, they lack direct experimental validation.

results.result: IL-12 and IL-18 may be involved in early AA development by stimulating IFN-γ production from resident IL-12Rβ2+ immune cells, and IL-12 is a key effector cytokine in promoting pathogenic IFN-γ secretion and immune privilege collapse.
results.evaluation: Claims C104-C106 are based on citations to published literature (Edelkamp, 2021) rather than data presented in this manuscript. While the authors used IL-12 and IL-18 to expand ILC1lc (C59), the specific role of these cytokines in AA pathogenesis is not directly tested in this study. These claims represent interesting hypotheses for future investigation but are not experimentally validated here.

results.result: AA is a common inflammatory hair loss disorder and autoimmune disease with major quality of life impact. Current therapy is unsatisfactory, and the exact pathobiology requires further characterization, including potential distinction between autoimmune (AAA) and non-autoimmune (NAIAA) variants.
results.evaluation: Claims C10-C19 are background/context claims supported by appropriate citations to published literature. These establish the clinical significance and rationale for the study. The claims are well-established in the field and appropriately referenced.

results.result: Prior work has established that AA lesions are associated with increased NKG2D+NK cells, that MICA is overexpressed in lesional AA hair follicles, that NKG2D and its ligands play a key role in AA, and that various innate immune cells including mast cells and γδ T cells are increased in AA and can induce AA hallmarks.
results.evaluation: Claims C20-C28 are background claims supported by appropriate citations to published literature, including the authors' own prior work. These establish the scientific context and rationale for investigating ILC1lc in AA. The claims are well-established in the field.

results.result: ILC1 cells are components of type 1 immunity that secrete IFN-γ, express NKG2D, are placed in strategic tissue locations, and play roles in various diseases. However, distinguishing ILC1 from NK cells is challenging, and the field lacks consensus on definitive markers.
results.evaluation: Claims C29-C50 are background claims about ILC1 biology supported by appropriate citations to published literature. These establish the scientific context for studying ILC1lc. The authors appropriately acknowledge the ongoing controversy about ILC1/NK distinction (C44, C45), which is a strength of the manuscript.

results.result: ILC1lc have been proposed to play immunopathology-initiating roles in other inflammatory conditions including vitiligo, IBD, lupus, and atherosclerosis. Abnormalities in ILC1lc-microbiota crosstalk have been observed in various diseases, and microbial dysbiosis has been reported in AA scalp skin.
results.evaluation: Claims C107, C109, C110 are supported by appropriate citations to published literature. These provide broader context for the potential role of ILC1lc in inflammatory diseases and suggest future research directions. The claims are appropriately presented as hypotheses for future investigation.

results.result: Innate/transitional immune cells play an important role in AA pathobiology.
results.evaluation: Claim C115 is a summary conclusion supported by the comprehensive experimental data presented in the manuscript showing that ILC1lc (an innate/transitional immune cell type) can induce all hallmarks of AA. This is a well-supported conclusion from the study.
